newsitem.title: USA: Checkpoint, Ultrak call off merger.
newsitem.headline: Checkpoint, Ultrak call off merger.

text.p: Checkpoint Systems Inc said Thursday that by mutual consent the agreement to merge with Ultrak Inc has been terminated.
The primary reason for the termination, said the company, was perceived "channel conflict" with Ultrak's large distributor and dealer network.
Checkpoint also said that it will not divest its closed circuit television division.

As announced on March 11, the merged company was to sell, install and service all Ultrak products through Ultrak's distribution network. But subsequent to the announcement, said the company, Checkpoint's retail customers expressed concern over this, saying they wanted to continue direct contact with Checkpoint during the sale, installation and servicing of closed circuit television (CCTV) systems.
Checkpoint said the two companies both came to the conclusion that Checkpoint will need to continue to market CCTV systems to retail customers through its own sales force.

"Unfortunately, the two companies also mutually agreed that selling CCTV systems direct to retail customers would create significant channel conflict with Ultrak's distributor/dealer network, which also sells, CCTV systems and other products to retail customers," the company said in a statement.
Based on each group's respective set of customers, Checkpoint said that it and Ultrak agreed that the expected synergies could not be accomplished.
"As a result of the termination, we will not divest our CCTV division," said Kevin P. Dowd, president and chief executive officer.

"In fact, we will continue to build on its capabilities. While we are disappointed that the merger did not materialize, through our due diligence process, we have seen an opportunity to become a dealer of Ultrak products to retail customers."
Wall Street arbitrage traders had valued the deal at $397 million.
Checkpoint said the stock options granted by Checkpoint and Ultrak to each other to acquire 19.9 percent of the common stock of the other company under certain conditions have also been terminated.
